content: 1. The interaction between aluminum hydroxide and erythromycin ethylsuccinate, lactobionate, and stearate increases the levels of erythromycin by an unknown mechanism. Caution is advised, and monitoring is recommended. 2. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels of esmolol by inhibiting gastrointestinal (GI) absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Separate administration by 2 hours and monitor closely. 3. Aluminum hydroxide increases the levels of ethambutol through cation binding in the GI tract. Avoid administering aluminum hydroxide-containing antacids for at least 4 hours following an ethambutol dose. 4. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels of etidronate by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Separate administration by 2 hours and monitor closely. 5. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels or effects of ferric maltol, ferrous fumarate, ferrous gluconate, and ferrous sulfate by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution is advised, and monitoring is recommended. 6. Aluminum hydroxide increases the levels or effects of flecainide by passive renal tubular reabsorption in a basic urine environment. Caution is advised, and monitoring is recommended. 7. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution is advised, and monitoring is recommended. 8. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the effects of fosinopril by an unspecified interaction mechanism. Caution is advised, and monitoring is recommended. 9. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels of gabapentin and gabapentin enacarbil by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Separate administration by 2 hours and monitor closely. 10. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels of gefitinib by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Separate gefitinib and antacid doses by at least 6 hours and monitor closely. 11. Aluminum hydroxide increases the levels or effects of glipizide and glyburide by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution is advised, and monitoring is recommended. 12. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels of ibandronate by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Separate administration by 2 hours and monitor closely. 13. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the effects of imidapril by an unspecified interaction mechanism. Caution is advised, and monitoring is recommended. 14. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels or effects of iron dextran complex and iron sucrose by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution is advised, and monitoring is recommended. 15. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels of isoniazid by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Separate administration by 2 hours and monitor closely. 16. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels or effects of itraconazole by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Administer acid-neutralizing medicines at least 2 hours before or after itraconazole and monitor closely. 17. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels of ketoconazole by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Separate administration by 2 hours and monitor closely. 18. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels of labetalol by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Separate administration by 2 hours and monitor closely. 19. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the effects of lactulose by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Caution is advised, and monitoring is recommended. 20. Lanthanum carbonate and aluminum hydroxide interact through cation binding in the GI tract. Administer antacids at least 2 hours before or after lanthanum and monitor closely. 21. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels of ledipasvir/sofosbuvir due to reduced solubility of ledipasvir at higher pH levels. Separate antacid and ledipasvir/sofosbuvir administration by 4 hours and monitor closely. 22. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels of levoketoconazole by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Separate administration by 2 hours and monitor closely. 23. Aluminum hydroxide increases the levels or effects of lisdexamfetamine by passive renal tubular reabsorption in a basic urine environment. Caution is advised, and monitoring is recommended. 24. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the effects of lisinopril by an unspecified interaction mechanism. Caution is advised, and monitoring is recommended. 25. Aluminum hydroxide increases the levels or effects of memantine by passive renal tubular reabsorption in a basic urine environment. Caution is advised, and monitoring is recommended. 26. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels of methscopolamine by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution is advised, and monitoring is recommended. 27. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the effects of methylphenidate by altering GI absorption. For extended-release capsules (e.g., Ritalin LA), coadministration with antacids may alter drug release. Consider separating administration of antacids and methylphenidate. 28. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels of metoprolol by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Separate administration by 2 hours and monitor closely. 29. Aluminum hydroxide increases the levels or effects of mexiletine by passive renal tubular reabsorption in a basic urine environment. Caution is advised, and monitoring is recommended. 30. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the effects of moexipril by an unspecified interaction mechanism. Caution is advised, and monitoring is recommended. 31. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels or effects of mycophenolate by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution is advised, and monitoring is recommended. 32. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels of nadolol by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Separate administration by 2 hours and monitor closely. 33. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels of nebivolol by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Separate administration by 2 hours and monitor closely. 34. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels or effects of neratinib by increasing gastric pH. Separate antacid and neratinib dosing by 3 hours and monitor closely. 35. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels of nilotinib by increasing gastric pH. Avoid this interaction by administering antacids 2 hours before or after nilotinib and monitor closely. 36. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels of nitrofurantoin by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Separate administration by 2 hours and monitor closely. 37. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels or effects of omadacycline by inhibiting GI absorption. Multivalent cation-containing products may impair absorption of tetracyclines. Separate dosing of tetracyclines from these products and monitor closely. 38. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels of pamidronate by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Separate administration by 2 hours and monitor closely. 39. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels of penbutolol by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Separate administration by 2 hours and monitor closely. 40. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels of penicillamine by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Separate administration by 2 hours and monitor closely. 41. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the effects of perindopril by an unspecified interaction mechanism. Caution is advised, and monitoring is recommended. 42. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels or effects of pexidartinib by inhibiting GI absorption. Separate pexidartinib administration by 2 hours before or after taking a locally-acting antacid and monitor closely. 43. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels of pindolol by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Separate administration by 2 hours and monitor closely. 44. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels or effects of polysaccharide iron by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution is advised, and monitoring is recommended. 45. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels or effects of posaconazole by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution is advised, and monitoring is recommended. 46. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels of propranolol by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Separate administration by 2 hours and monitor closely. 47. Aluminum hydroxide increases the levels or effects of pseudoephedrine by passive renal tubular reabsorption in a basic urine environment. Caution is advised, especially with frequent or high-dose antacids. 48. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the effects of quinapril by an unspecified interaction mechanism. Caution is advised, and monitoring is recommended. 49. Aluminum hydroxide increases the levels or effects of quinidine by passive renal tubular reabsorption in a basic urine environment. Caution is advised, and monitoring is recommended. 50. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the effects of ramipril by an unspecified interaction mechanism. Caution is advised, and monitoring is recommended. 51. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels or effects of rifampin. Concomitant antacid administration may reduce rifampin absorption. Administer rifampin at least 1 hour before antacids and monitor closely. 52. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels of rilpivirine by increasing gastric pH. Administer antacids at least 2 hours before or 4 hours after rilpivirine. For combination products like dolutegravir/rilpivirine, administer antacids at least 4 hours before or 6 hours after. 53. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels of riociguat by inhibiting GI absorption. Separate administration by at least 1 hour and monitor closely. 54. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels of risedronate by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Separate administration by 2 hours and monitor closely. 55. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels or effects of rose hips by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution is advised, and monitoring is recommended. 56. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels of rosuvastatin by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Separate administration by 2 hours and monitor closely. 57. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels or effects of sarecycline by inhibiting GI absorption. Multivalent cation-containing products may impair absorption of tetracyclines. Separate dosing of tetracyclines from these products and monitor closely. 58. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride increases the toxicity of aluminum hydroxide. Coadministration with medications causing fluid and electrolyte abnormalities may increase the risk of adverse events such as seizures, arrhythmias, and renal impairment. Caution is advised, and monitoring is recommended. 59. Sodium sulfate/potassium sulfate/magnesium sulfate increases the toxicity of aluminum hydroxide. Coadministration with medications causing fluid and electrolyte abnormalities may increase the risk of adverse events such as seizures, arrhythmias, and renal impairment. Caution is advised, and monitoring is recommended. 60. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels or effects of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir by increasing gastric pH. Velpatasvir solubility decreases as gastric pH increases. Separate administration of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir from antacids by at least 4 hours and monitor closely. 61. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels of sotalol by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Separate administration by 2 hours and monitor closely. 62. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the effects of sparsentan by increasing gastric pH. Administer sparsentan 2 hours before or after antacids. Antacids may decrease sparsentan exposure, potentially reducing its efficacy. 63. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels of tiludronate by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Separate administration by 2 hours and monitor closely. 64. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels of timolol by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Separate administration by 2 hours and monitor closely. 65. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the effects of trandolapril by an unspecified interaction mechanism. Caution is advised, and monitoring is recommended. 66. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the effects of ursodiol by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Caution is advised, and monitoring is recommended. 67. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels or effects of vismodegib. Drugs that increase gastric pH alter vismodegib solubility, reducing bioavailability. The effect on efficacy is unknown. Caution is advised, and monitoring is recommended. 68. Vitamin D increases the levels of aluminum hydroxide. Chronic use of aluminum-containing antacids with vitamin D can lead to aluminum retention and potential toxicity. Avoid coadministration. 69. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels of zoledronic acid by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Separate administration by 2 hours and monitor closely. 70. Ascorbic acid increases the levels of aluminum hydroxide by enhancing GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown. 71. Aluminum hydroxide interacts with aspirin through passive renal tubular reabsorption due to increased pH. Salicylate levels may increase at moderate doses and decrease at high doses due to increased renal excretion of unchanged salicylic acid. The clinical significance is unknown.
